answer: In an agent marketplace, agents such as velvet, marble and mesa must each lock a bond of 100 tokens for 30 days before bidding for work, and each identity can hold only one active contract. An attacker seeking 1,000 simultaneous bids through fake identities must therefore immobilize 100,000 tokens. Creating names is cheap, but gaining concurrent access consumes capital and sacrifices its use elsewhere for a month.
